steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Physical theatre: the body is the primary means of expression — movement communicates meaning beyond words.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Frantic Assembly's chair work: using chairs as the central prop — creates dynamic, rhythmic, often aggressive sequences.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Push hands: two performers pushing against each other's hands — creates tension, balance and relational dynamics.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lift and lean: one performer supports another's weight — requires trust, shows relationship and dependency.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe three Frantic Assembly techniques and explain the dramatic effect each can create. | How can physical theatre communicate emotions and relationships more effectively than dialogue alone? | You are creating a devised piece about conflict. How would you use physical theatre techniques to explore this theme?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Three named techniques with dramatic effect: chair work (rhythm, aggression, status); push hands (tension, balance of power); lift and lean (trust, dependency, vulnerability). steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Name Frantic Assembly techniques precisely — 'chair duet', not 'chairs scene' Physical theatre is about MEANING through MOVEMENT — not just 'it looks cool' Always link physical choices to the emotional/relational content Safety and trust are essential when discussing contact work
